parsed_response.reasoning: The diff literally defines `minimumTokenResponseSchema` with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`; `z.string().toString()` evaluates to a meaningless string (a ZodString's toString), not a dynamic key, so those schema entries are inert and only `access_token` is enforced. The comment in the same block says 'Assume that any property with a number is the expiry', but nothing requires an expiry, so a sync-enabled refresh response lacking expiry passes validation and downstream `expiry_date` stays undefined (e.g. in googlecalendar CalendarService, `googleCredentials.expiry_date = token.expiry_date`), meaning the token is never considered expired. This is a verifiable defect in newly added code.

judged_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, which evaluate to the literal key "[object Object]"-style strings, so the schema enforces nothing beyond access_token and is structurally meaningless. Every sync-enabled refresh accepts any object containing an access_token (comments imply an expiry number should be required); a response missing expiry leaves expiry_date undefined, googleCredentials.expiry_date becomes undefined, and the token is treated as never-expiring so it is never refreshed again until the API starts returning 401s on user booking paths.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]`, which evaluates to a single literal property name (whatever `toString()` returns, typically a "[object Object]"-style string), not “any string key”. This makes the schema logically wrong (it won’t enforce “any numeric expiry field” as the comment suggests, and may even reject normal token responses if that literal key is absent). This is a real correctness defect introduced by the diff. (The finding’s downstream behavior description about “accepts any object with access_token”/never-expiring tokens isn’t fully verifiable from the diff, but the schema construction itself is plainly incorrect.)
